case_title: Kala Singh @ Gurnam Singh v. State of Punjab
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (drank together); prior dispute over alleged theft of the appellant's pigeon
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 and s.201 (charged); final conviction under IPC s.304 Part II r/w s.34 and s.201
evidence_type: Chemical examiner report; other evidence and material on record (testimony not detailed in the judgment)
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight in heat of passion over sudden quarrel; no pre-meditation; no intention to cause death; counsel submitted appellant had served over three years
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302/34 and 201 IPC; life rigorous imprisonment (s.302/34) and 3 years RI (s.201), plus fine
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 713 DB of 2003) partly allowed: conviction altered to s.304 Part I r/w s.34; 12 years RI and Rs.10,000 fine; s.201 conviction maintained
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part II r/w s.34 (culpable homicide); IPC s.201
neutral_facts: On the day in question, the accused, a co-accused and the victim obtained a bottle of liquor from a house and went to a bridge over a minor canal, where they drank it. A quarrel broke out between the accused and the victim, the accused alleging that the victim had stolen the accused's pigeon. The scuffle took place on the spur of the moment. During the scuffle the co-accused, who was carrying a rod, struck the victim on the head with it. The victim fell down and did not respond even after about half an hour. The accused and the co-accused then moved the body and placed it in a minor canal. The incident occurred one day before panchayat elections. Evidence on record included a chemical examiner's report showing that the victim had consumed liquor, along with other material on record describing the sudden nature of the fight.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a rod blow to the head; body then placed in minor canal
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld in modified form (s.304 Part II/34 substituted for s.302/34, and s.201)
financial_property_loss: Alleged theft of the appellant's pigeon; no monetary value stated
premeditation_planning: Court found no premeditation; the quarrel and scuffle arose on the spur of the moment
motive: Quarrel over alleged theft of the appellant's pigeon (sudden quarrel accepted on the evidence)
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence on record showing a sudden scuffle without intention to kill; chemical examiner report showing deceased had consumed liquor (as noted by High Court)
post_offence_conduct: Body shifted to the minor canal after the blow when there was no response for half an hour
custody_duration: Not stated (counsel submitted the appellant had served more than three years of sentence)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 08.02.2019 and 01.03.2019; Supreme Court: 21.09.2021
legal_representation: Appellant: Bharat Sood, P. S. Sudheer, Advocates. State of Punjab: Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Ms. Mandakini Singh, Karanvir Gogia, Ms. Shivangi Singhal, Ms. Ashima Mandla, Advocates
investigation_status: Trial completed; accused convicted by Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted ss.302/34 and 201, life RI. High Court: s.302 altered to s.304 Part I r/w s.34, 12 years RI, s.201 maintained. Supreme Court: s.304 Part II r/w s.34, 7 years RI, fine maintained, s.201 maintained
prosecution_argument: No grounds to interfere with conviction or sentence; leniency already shown; Uday Singh distinguishable on facts
defence_argument: No intention to kill; sudden fight in heat of passion; High Court should have convicted under s.304 Part II, not Part I (relying on Uday Singh); request to reduce sentence given over three years served
legal_principle_applied: Absence of intention to cause death or such bodily injury as likely to cause death, with sudden fight in heat of passion, warrants conviction under s.304 Part II rather than Part I
precedent_relied_upon: Uday Singh v. State of U.P. (2002) 7 SCC 79; Shahajan Ali & Ors. etc. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. etc. (2017) 11 SC 807
sentencing_rationale: Conversion to s.304 Part II reflected the absence of intention to kill and the sudden fight; the judgment gives no separate sentencing reasoning for seven years
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden fight in heat of passion upon sudden quarrel; no pre-meditation; no intention to cause death
other_sentence_order: Rs.10,000 fine (s.304 Part II/34) maintained; s.201 conviction, 3 years RI and Rs.500 fine maintained
